claims.text: Wright-Patterson AFB was formally established on 13 January 1948 by consolidating Wright Field, Patterson Field, Dayton Army Air Field and Clinton Army Air Field.

claims.text: The National Air and Space Intelligence Center, the direct institutional successor to ATIC and the Foreign Technology Division, is headquartered at Wright-Patterson AFB.

edges.label: ATIC and its successors were and are headquartered at Wright-Patterson
edges.note: The Air Technical Intelligence Center, formed in 1951 from Air Materiel Command's T-2 intelligence organisation at Wright Field, became the Foreign Technology Division in 1961 and NASIC in 1993, which remains at the base. Attested by USAF unit histories.

edges.label: The Bolender memo closed the base's public reporting channel while conceding another existed
edges.note: Brig. Gen. Carroll Bolender's 1969 memorandum recommended Blue Book's termination and stated that reports which could affect national security were never part of the Blue Book system - a statement about this base's own reporting architecture.

edges.label: Twining wrote the 1947 AMC assessment from this command
edges.note: Lt. Gen. Nathan Twining signed 'AMC Opinion Concerning Flying Discs' on 23 September 1947 as commander of Air Materiel Command, headquartered at Wright Field.

a.label: National Air and Space Intelligence Center

edges.label: NASIC is the current tenant institution at Wright-Patterson
edges.note: The National Air and Space Intelligence Center is a Wright-Patterson tenant and the direct institutional heir to ATIC/FTD's foreign materiel exploitation mission.

edges.label: Blue Book was hosted at Wright-Patterson from 1952 to 1969
edges.note: Project Blue Book, like SIGN and GRUDGE before it, was hosted at this base under ATIC. Of 12,618 sightings studied, 701 remained unexplained at closure. Attested by USAF fact sheets.
